Public specification:
Build a 4-digit BCD (binary-coded decimal) counter. Each decimal digit is encoded using 4 bits: q[3:0] is the ones digit, q[7:4] is the tens digit, etc. For digits [3:1], also output an enable signal indicating when each of the upper three digits should be incremented. Include a synchronous active-high reset.

Input widths {'reset': 1}; output widths {'ena': 3, 'q': 16}. Clock clk; sample after the posedge edge has settled. Each row's values are driven before the sampled edge. Optional mid input changes occur AFTER sampling, before the other edge, and are carried to the start of the next row. Protocol seed 20261120.
Return only executable Python with function reference(vectors). For each row return a dictionary with every output and a concrete unsigned integer within that output's bit width, even when power-up is unspecified. Preserve timing and process mid changes at the correct point. No imports, classes, prints, external files or executable code outside functions. Comments may label the contract rules.
Veri-Sure contract:
{"module_name":"top_module","io":[{"name":"clk","dir":"input","width":1,"description":"Clock; counter samples on posedge."},{"name":"reset","dir":"input","width":1,"description":"Synchronous active-high reset."},{"name":"q","dir":"output","width":16,"description":"4-digit BCD counter value: q[3:0]=ones, q[7:4]=tens, q[11:8]=hundreds, q[15:12]=thousands."},{"name":"ena","dir":"output","width":3,"description":"Enable signals for upper digits: ena[0]=tens enable, ena[1]=hundreds enable, ena[2]=thousands enable."}],"clocking":{"clock":{"name":"clk","edge":"posedge"},"reset":{"name":"reset","active":"high","kind":"synchronous"}},"timing":{"outputs":{"q":{"latency_cycles":1},"ena":{"latency_cycles":1}}},"functional_summary":{"overview":"4-digit BCD counter with synchronous active-high reset. Each decimal digit is 4 bits; q[3:0] is ones, q[7:4] tens, q[11:8] hundreds, q[15:12] thousands. ena[0] indicates tens digit increments, ena[1] hundreds, ena[2] thousands.","rules":["On posedge clk: if reset is high, q <= 0 and ena <= 0.","Otherwise, ones digit q[3:0] increments by 1 each cycle, wrapping 9->0.","ena[0] is asserted when the tens digit should increment, i.e., when ones digit is 9 (about to wrap).","ena[1] is asserted when the hundreds digit should increment, i.e., when ones=9 and tens=9.","ena[2] is asserted when the thousands digit should increment, i.e., when ones=9, tens=9, and hundreds=9.","Each digit increments modulo 10 independently based on its enable condition; the full 4-digit value wraps 9999->0000.","ena outputs reflect the enable conditions computed from the current (pre-edge) counter state, registered on the same posedge as q."]}}
response:
```python
def reference(vectors):
    # Contract: synchronous active-high reset; outputs registered on posedge.
    # ena reflects enable conditions computed from pre-edge state, registered same edge.
    # q[3:0]=ones, q[7:4]=tens, q[11:8]=hundreds, q[15:12]=thousands.
    # ena[0]=tens enable (ones==9), ena[1]=hundreds enable (ones==9 & tens==9),
    # ena[2]=thousands enable (ones==9 & tens==9 & hundreds==9).
    # Power-up unspecified -> start at 0.
    q = 0
    ena = 0
    out = []
    for row in vectors:
        # Apply inputs driven before the sampled edge
        reset = row.get('reset', 0)
        # Compute next state based on current (pre-edge) state
        ones = q & 0xF
        tens = (q >> 4) & 0xF
        hundreds = (q >> 8) & 0xF
        thousands = (q >> 12) & 0xF

        if reset:
            nq = 0
            nena = 0
        else:
            e0 = 1 if ones == 9 else 0
            e1 = 1 if (ones == 9 and tens == 9) else 0
            e2 = 1 if (ones == 9 and tens == 9 and hundreds == 9) else 0
            nena = (e2 << 2) | (e1 << 1) | e0

            nones = (ones + 1) % 10
            ntens = (tens + e0) % 10
            nhundreds = (hundreds + e1) % 10
            nthousands = (thousands + e2) % 10
            nq = (nthousands << 12) | (nhundreds << 8) | (ntens << 4) | nones

        # Sample after posedge settled
        q = nq
        ena = nena
        out.append({'q': q, 'ena': ena})
    return out
```
